insights.headline: SEBI-linked gold fund curbs widen ahead of Diwali as RBI burns $60 billion defending the rupee
insights.summary: India tightened the screws on gold demand this week: seventeen mutual fund houses halted fresh investments into gold ETF fund-of-funds from October 15-16, days before Diwali, while the Finance Ministry cut duty drawback rates on jewellery exports. The RBI's forex reserves fell roughly $60 billion in six weeks to $726 billion as it sold dollars to prop up the rupee. Globally, spot gold held near $4,170 an ounce, caught between fading bets on an immediate Fed rate hike and Treasury yields lifted by Brent crude at $110 a barrel.
points: 17 fund houses halted fresh gold ETF FoF inflows from Oct 15-16; existing SIPs, redemptions and direct ETF buying stay open.
Gold ETF inflows jumped 71% in September to ₹4,450.61 crore — the strongest since January — before the curbs.
RBI forex reserves fell ~$60 billion in six weeks to $726.03 billion; gold reserves dipped $1.32 billion to $105.09 billion.
Spot gold held near $4,170/oz; traders cut October Fed-hike odds to ~15% after Chair Warsh's Bangkok remarks.
Duty drawback on gold jewellery exports cut 3.1% to ₹1,794.11/g; silver cut ~9% to ₹26,859.02/kg.

trending.title: Diwali-season squeeze on gold demand
trending.summary: Fund houses halted fresh gold FoF money ahead of Diwali while the bullion import duty sits at 15% since May, squeezing festival demand. Retailers answer with lighter pieces and exchange offers.

trending.title: Rupee defence is getting expensive
trending.summary: The RBI burned ~$60 billion of reserves in six weeks against high crude, rising US yields and $26.8 billion of FPI outflows. Gold imports, down 81%, remain a watched dollar drain.

trending.title: Gold stuck in a $4,100-$4,200 corridor
trending.summary: Sticky US inflation keeps Fed tightening bets alive to cap rallies, while $110 Brent and safe-haven bids hold the floor. Gold ended near $4,170 with central-bank buying cushioning the downside.

trending.title: Silver's wilder ride
trending.summary: down 50% from its January record and ~20% off its August high, with solar demand failing to cushion the fall; domestic silver still slid ₹10,191 this week.

trending.title: Trade policy tightening at the margins
trending.summary: The drawback cut trims exporter refunds and GJC is fighting the 67% hallmarking fee hike — two small steps that together raise the cost of moving metal through formal channels.

items.title: Curbs on gold funds widen as rupee, reserves face pressure
items.summary: Seventeen fund houses stopped fresh investments into gold ETF fund-of-funds from October 15-16 — the second clampdown this year. Lump-sum investments, switch-ins and new SIP/STP registrations are halted; existing SIPs, redemptions and direct ETF buying stay open. The move lands days before Diwali, after September gold ETF inflows jumped 71% to ₹4,450.61 crore.

items.title: Gold Falls ₹3,000 This Week, Silver Slides Over ₹10,000
items.summary: IBJA data showed 24-carat gold falling ₹3,004 over the week to ₹1,46,426 per 10 grams and silver sliding ₹10,191 to ₹2,10,918 per kg; spot gold traded near $4,186 and silver near $57 as rising crude lifted the dollar.

items.title: $60 billion in 6 weeks: RBI's rupee defence comes at a cost
items.summary: India's forex reserves fell roughly $60 billion in six weeks to $726.03 billion on October 9, down from a record $785.71 billion, as the RBI sold dollars to defend the rupee. The latest week alone saw an $8.58 billion drawdown amid high crude prices, rising US yields and foreign capital outflows. India's gold reserves also slipped $1.32 billion to $105.09 billion in the week to October 8.

items.title: Gold steady near $4,170 as easing Fed rate-hike bets counter high oil prices and yields
items.summary: Spot gold held near $4,170 an ounce on Friday after Thursday's 1.6% jump — its sharpest gain in over two weeks. Cooling expectations of a Fed hike — Chair Warsh declined in Bangkok to signal tightening — offset a crude rally that lifted Treasury yields, with Brent at $110. Gold ended the week unchanged as mid-week safe-haven gains were countered by hotter US inflation data.

items.title: Gold imports plunge 81% to 30-month low; ICRA sees CAD widening to 0.9% of GDP
items.summary: India's gold imports plunged 81.3% year-on-year to $1.8 billion in September — the lowest in 30 months — helping narrow the merchandise trade deficit to $30.2 billion from $33 billion, Commerce Ministry data showed. The $7.8 billion drop in the gold bill more than offset higher oil and electronics imports. ICRA said the easing was non-oil driven and forecast the CAD at 0.9% of GDP in FY27.

items.title: Gold's Split Screen: Sticky Inflation on One Side, Central-Bank Buying on the Other
items.summary: Gold closed the session at $4,169.08, holding near weekly support after Thursday's rebound: a softer dollar and falling Treasury yields offset the September CPI shock (3.7% headline, 2.6% core) that firmed October hike bets. Speculators had already trimmed net-long positions before the data landed, while steady central-bank buying continues to cushion the downside.

items.title: Govt cuts gold duty drawback rate by 3.1 pc, silver by nearly 9 pc
items.summary: The Finance Ministry cut duty drawback rates on gold and silver jewellery exports: gold jewellery drops 3.1% from ₹1,851.99 to ₹1,794.11 per gram, silver jewellery falls about 9% from ₹29,501.09 to ₹26,859.02 per kg, under an October 15 notification. The cut trims duty refunds on imported inputs, squeezing exporter margins.

items.title: GJC urges Govt, BIS to review 67% hike in gold hallmarking charges amid compliance concerns
items.summary: GJC has urged the government and BIS to review the 67% hike in gold hallmarking charges — from ₹45 to ₹75 per article, notified September 14 — calling it unwarranted while fake hallmarking persists. With over 60 crore articles hallmarked since 2021, the council argues scale should have contained costs and wants enforcement prioritised over higher fees.

items.title: Silver's recent 50% drop from a record high hints that an economic slowdown looms
items.summary: Silver futures touched a record intraday $121.79 an ounce in late January, per Dow Jones Market Data, and have since lost more than half, settling at $57.31 on Friday. Dealers told MarketWatch that silver's dual monetary-industrial role makes its weakness a leading indicator of economic trouble as high energy prices bite. Gold has fallen more than 25% from its own January record of $5,626.80.

items.title: [SMM Analysis] Silver Down Nearly 20% From Stage High: Why Are Solar Cell Prices Not Following?
items.summary: SMM's #1 silver price fell 19.6% from its August 27 high of 16,889 yuan/kg to 13,584 yuan/kg on October 15, edging to 13,842 yuan/kg on the 16th. Yet solar cell prices barely budged: M10 cell costs fell 10.8% to 0.310 yuan/W while G12R prices held flat since September 18. SMM blames hawkish Fed minutes, a dollar index above 102 and multi-year-high yields; COMEX silver broke below $60 on October 8.

items.title: Lighter pieces, smarter buys: What jewellers are betting on this festive season
items.summary: With gold near ₹1.5 lakh per 10 grams, jewellers are redesigning for the festive season: lighter pieces, wider carat choices and old-gold exchange — now 45-50% of business at Senco Gold and over half of Titan's purchases. Senco's Suvankar Sen says budgets rose ~20% while prices doubled, forcing 30-40% weight cuts; Titan is pushing modular wedding designs and 18-carat pieces.

items.title: RBI fixes SGB 2020-21 Series VII premature redemption price at Rs 14,614; exit window on October 19
items.summary: The RBI fixed the premature redemption price of Sovereign Gold Bond 2020-21 Series VII at Rs 14,614 per unit — about a 192% capital gain for digital subscribers who paid Rs 5,001 in October 2020. The exit window was moved to October 19 because October 20 is a Dussehra holiday. Holders can also stay until the October 2028 maturity and keep collecting 2.5% annual interest.

items.title: Brent crude hits $110 a barrel for first time since May as supply concerns mount
items.summary: Brent crude touched $110 a barrel for the first time since May on October 17 as Iran-related supply fears intensified, before easing back toward $105. Costlier oil lifts inflation expectations and US yields — a headwind for gold — and pressures the rupee, which raises the landed cost of gold in India.

items.title: Bullion Cues: Weakness may deepen
items.summary: Gold ($4,165.40) and silver ($57) lost 0.7% and 6.3% last week; MCX gold futures (₹1,47,918) fell 2.4% and silver (₹2,11,187) 6.5%. The Hindu BusinessLine's research bureau says MCX gold must cross ₹1,51,700 to turn positive, with supports at ₹1,43,500 and ₹1,41,000; silver could slide to the ₹2,00,000–2,00,750 band unless it reclaims ₹2,28,000–2,30,000.

items.title: India Bullion: Up on weak dollar; market assesses Fed rate outlook
items.summary: MCX December gold rose 0.6% to ₹1,48,320 per 10 grams and December silver gained 1.4% to ₹2,13,570 per kg on Friday as the dollar index fell to a two-week low of 101.57; COMEX gold was up 0.6% at $4,195.3 and silver up 1.5% at $57.99. Kotak Securities cited safe-haven flows from the equity selloff, while Commerzbank said Fed Chair Warsh's comments further dented October hike expectations.

items.title: Sensex gains 414 points; MCX gold up 0.64% to Rs 1,48,429, silver up 1.33% to Rs 2,13,460 on Friday
items.summary: MCX bullion futures rebounded on Friday: December gold rose 0.64% to Rs 1,48,429 per 10 grams and December silver gained 1.33% to Rs 2,13,460 per kg, after a weak week. The bounce tracked softer US bond yields and a weaker dollar, though the rupee's gains capped the domestic move. Brent eased to about $105 after touching $110.

items.title: Gold on Dhanteras: celebrate the ritual, rethink the investment
items.summary: A Mint column argues Dhanteras gold buying should be treated as ritual rather than investing: jewellery's making charges vanish on resale and coins sit in rented lockers, making festive gold consumption rather than a financial plan.
